editorNote: This issue follows the last week of September 1982 into the first October chart date: Atari VCS shelves fill with licensed and third-party games, Apple II owners keep buying arcade and fantasy titles, and Commodore's 64K machine keeps changing the price conversation.
morningLine: M-Network turns a Data East maze chase into an Atari VCS shelf story while Jack & Diane takes over the radio and E.T. keeps ruling theaters.

lead.headline: Lock 'n' Chase Joins the Atari VCS Maze Rush
lead.summary: Mattel's M-Network brought Data East's Lock 'n' Chase to the Atari VCS in October 1982, giving Atari owners another arcade-style maze game just as third-party console shelves were becoming crowded. The cartridge put a thief, police pursuit, doors, and gold bars into the home-console aisle, and it showed how aggressively Intellivision's parent company was now chasing Atari households with software.
lead.confidence: Lock 'n' Chase is listed as an October 1982 M-Network Atari 2600 release; used as exact-month shelf context for this weekly issue
